description: One cup of granulated sugar weighs 198 grams. Many charts round it to 200, but King Arthur says 198. Convert sugar between cups and grams, with the table.

steps: Multiply by the weight of one cup: 2 × 198 g.

examples.result: 300 g of granulated sugar = 1.52 cups, about 1 1/2 cups.
steps: Divide by the weight of one cup: 300 ÷ 198.

faqs.answer: 198 grams. That is the figure on King Arthur Baking's ingredient weight chart, 7 ounces per cup.
faqs.question: How many grams are in a cup of granulated sugar?

faqs.answer: They round up. 198 is close enough to 200 that plenty of charts simplify it, and for one cup the difference never matters. Across several cups it adds up, so this page uses the chart figure: 198.
faqs.question: Why do some charts say 200 grams?
How many cups is 500 g of granulated sugar?

faqs.answer: 16 tablespoons, each about 12.4 grams. A level tablespoon is the way to measure small amounts without the scale.
faqs.question: How many tablespoons are in a cup of sugar?

faqs.answer: No. A packed cup of brown sugar weighs 213 grams, because the molasses adds moisture and the packing squeezes out the air. A cup of granulated sugar is 198 grams.

felicityNote: I used to round sugar to 200 grams a cup like everyone else. Then a five-cup jam recipe taught me what 10 grams of rounding tastes like.

parts.meaning: The volume in the recipe, measured spooned and levelled.
The grams in one cup of granulated sugar, from King Arthur Baking's chart.
The weight on the scale. It does not change with how you fill the cup.

howToSteps.name: Spoon it into the cup
howToSteps.text: Spoon the sugar into the measuring cup until it heaps over the top. The crystals settle evenly, so there is no fluffing step the way there is with flour.

howToSteps.name: Level it off
howToSteps.text: Sweep the flat edge of a knife across the rim of the cup, back into the bag. The cup is now level and holds one cup.

howToSteps.name: Use the tablespoon for small amounts
howToSteps.text: For a tablespoon or two, measure with a tablespoon and level it the same way. One level tablespoon of granulated sugar weighs 12.4 grams.

howToSteps.name: Convert or weigh
howToSteps.text: Weigh the sugar if you have a scale: one level cup should read 198 grams. Or use the converter above. Cups times 198 is grams, grams divided by 198 is cups.

name: Granulated Sugar
sourceNote: King Arthur Baking lists granulated white sugar at 198 g per cup (7 oz).
title: Cups to Grams: Granulated Sugar
tutorial: Sugar is the most honest cup in the pantry. The crystals are all the same size and they settle the same way every time, so a cup of granulated sugar weighs 198 grams whether you spoon it in or scoop it. No fluffing, no levelling anxiety. It just lands on the number.

The number comes from King Arthur Baking's ingredient weight chart: 198 grams per cup, 7 ounces. Plenty of charts round that to 200 grams, and the rounding is the trap on this page. Two grams a cup sounds like nothing. Across five cups it is 10 grams, which is nearly a tablespoon of sugar you never meant to add.

Measure it spooned and levelled like anything else. Spoon the sugar into the cup until it heaps, then sweep a knife across the rim. Sugar does not pack down the way flour does, so the method matters less here, but a level cup is still the cup the chart means.
The converter works in both directions. Cups become grams when you want the scale. Grams become cups when the recipe is in grams. Both directions use the same number: 198 grams per cup.

The anchor is the half cup. Half a cup is 99 grams, near enough 100 grams that you can round it in your head. Two cups is 396 grams. One tablespoon is 12.4 grams. Once the half cup anchor is in your head, most recipes convert themselves.
